title: The Hundred Days
subtitle: Belgium, June 1815 — the road to Waterloo
intro: Napoleon has escaped Elba and retaken France. Two armies stand between him and Brussels: Wellington's Anglo-Allied army and Blücher's Prussians. His plan is to strike between them, defeat each in turn, and end the war before Austria and Russia arrive. Every regiment you lose now will be missing at Waterloo.

grouchy.title: Marshal Grouchy
grouchy.text: Morning, 17 June. Blücher's beaten army slipped away in the night and nobody saw which road it took. The Emperor turns on Wellington and gives the right wing to Marshal Grouchy. What are his orders?

options.label: Pursue the Prussians
options.text: As history. Grouchy follows Blücher to Wavre with III and IV Corps: Habert, Lefol, Berthezène, Pécheux, the 12e tirailleurs and the 1er Lanciers miss Waterloo. The Prussians reach the field 40-60 minutes later, without Pirch I's brigade and their uhlans.
options.brief: Grouchy is pursuing the Prussians: they will come late and weaker, but his regiments are not here.

options.label: Screen them lightly
options.text: A division and the light horse keep contact: Pécheux and the 1er Lanciers miss Waterloo. The Prussians are slowed by 20-30 minutes.
options.brief: Grouchy is screening the Prussians with a light force: they will be slowed a little.

options.label: March to the sound of the guns
options.text: Every regiment fights at Waterloo, and Gérard's IV Corps follows the cannon fire to arrive about six in the evening. Nothing holds the Prussians back.
options.brief: Grouchy is marching to the sound of the guns: Gérard's corps should arrive about six. The Prussians come on time.

endings.waterloo_win: The Coalition line breaks. Wellington withdraws toward the coast and Blücher falls back on the Rhine. Without a decisive allied victory the coalition falters — Napoleon enters Brussels and offers terms. The Hundred Days become something longer.
endings.waterloo_draw: Night falls over a bloodied field. Neither army has broken, but the Prussians are on the flank and the Emperor's reserves are gone. The campaign will be decided by the retreat.
endings.waterloo_loss: The Guard recoils, the line dissolves, and the cry goes up: 'La Garde recule!' Napoleon abdicates for the second time and is sent to Saint Helena. History is kept.
